description: Postgres shrink via ingest repoint to Parquet — bridge, then cut per lane

supersedes.parquet_duckdb_pivot_20260823: item E of RUNBOOK 0.33.3 (forward path per lane, upstream -> Parquet) moves here; items A (slice d1), C (d3), D (d4) stay there and are this track's external dependencies

external_dependencies.for: coarse-rung derivation fix, signal z13 re-export with positions, retraction of the 2026-08-08..16 signal absences; blocks s5 exporter deletion

partitions.note: Prebaked from the planning analysis at 440d9b5; no separate recon pass. Excludes every path owned by parquet_duckdb_pivot_20260823 slices d0-d5. lane_registry.py, cli.py, alembic/versions/ and the cron Dockerfile are shared registries with one named owner each: later slices append and must be sequenced, never run concurrently on those files. Re-verify `owns` with a real grep once HEAD moves. RE-VERIFIED at 80ac72a (RUNBOOK 0.42.15): every `owns` path grepped against HEAD -- no drift, every `future` path genuinely absent and every existing one present. s2/s3/s4 overlap on pipeline/direct/ and tests/direct/ (directory owner vs files inside it) but are SEQUENCED by depends_on and all sit in lane A, so that is ordering, not contention. The one real collision is external: pivot d5 creates pipeline/lanes/soil_field.py inside s5's directory -- d5 moves to lane A and lands first. s2 EXPANDED 2026-08-25 to absorb the cli.py split (owner request): 4,215 lines, 57 commands, 73 private helpers, 12 raw text() SQL calls on the CLI surface. Precedent already exists -- five modules define click commands outside cli.py and @cli.group('local') is already a group.

slices.task: P0 bridge: restore cronSchedule so a writer runs on a clock again; correct the Dockerfile header (it still claims the schedule was removed on purpose and that continuous-warehouse-loop.sh replaces it); verify the drain stays down.

P1 alembic greenfield baseline: one revision reflecting production as-is (no timescaledb, tracking.positions plain), archive the historical revisions, re-point every migration-contract test, move the readiness pin, stamp production. Fallback to a forward migration if the agri-schema pg_dump diff is non-empty.

P2 direct-writer foundation, now FOLDED WITH THE CLI SPLIT (owner decision 2026-08-25). Runs as two sequenced sub-slices under one owner of cli.py, because a 4,215-line split and a new verb cannot be reviewed as one unit: s2a = split cli.py into interface/cli/ groups forecast|ml|data|ops, RENAME the binary agri-cli -> agri-service with a HARD CUTOVER (no aliases), and lift business logic out of the CLI surface per agri_sdk_layering phases 4-8; s2b = the direct-writer protocol, the parity harness, the parquet-ingest verb and the lane->writer registry, plus wave 1 lanes sensors and weather-observations, built INTO the new structure so nothing is written twice.
slices.note: HARD CUTOVER HAZARDS, all four must move in the SAME change as the rename. (1) infra/cron-ingest/Dockerfile:108 ENTRYPOINT names three verbs (ingest-all, jobs-pulse, parquet-gap-fill). (2) infra/cron-mtbs/railway.json:10 startCommand. (3) infra/parquet-drain/railway.json:9 -- AND THAT SERVICE IS SOURCE-DISCONNECTED, so it will NOT redeploy: its start command must be corrected now or it breaks silently the day someone reconnects it for d1's ladder repair. (4) a dashboard-set startCommand can override the file (see memory plantgeo-cron-service-dockerfile-path) -- verify in the Railway dashboard, not just in the repo. Also: the deploy carrying s0's restored cronSchedule must carry the renamed binary and the new ENTRYPOINT together; they ship in one image, so that part is atomic. ML NAMING RESOLVED: method/ml/ stays the module home (phases 0-3 already shipped it); `agri-service ml` is a VERB GROUP, not a module path, so the conflict agri_sdk_layering left open does not bind here. interface/cli/ mirrors interface/http/, which lane B created at 273828b.

slices.task: P3 wave 2 direct writers: drought, water-gauges, fire-perimeters, burn-severity, watersheds, evacuation-zones, and the soil-survey decision; replace the three Postgres-backed static-lookup watermark resolvers with an upstream vintage or record that a lane keeps its Postgres watermark.

P4 wave 3 direct writers for the governance-heavy lanes: signal (governed contract table + release dedup + centroid), vegetation (eight lineage refs), fire-detections (cell-day aggregate + FIRMS cap surfaced).

P5 per-lane Postgres retirement: delete each verified lane's ingest producer and runner registration, switch the cron entrypoint to parquet-ingest for verified lanes, drop the lane tables as migrations on the s1 baseline. Exporter deletion waits on pivot d1.
slices.note: Does NOT own pipeline/lanes/soil_field.py -- pivot d5 creates it and must land first (RUNBOOK 0.42.15). Retire a lane's producer only after that lane's parity passes; soil-field has no Postgres producer to retire.

slices.task: P6 final shrink: drop the signal unique CONSTRAINT (10.78 GB), the remaining signal indexes, then agri.signal_observation; then the geo.features/geo.geometry data-plane rows for retired lanes via a drizzle migration. Gated on pivot d3 and d4.

tripwires: s0: never restart plantgeo-parquet-drain or continuous-warehouse-loop.sh; every push auto-deploys the cron and runs one pass immediately; restartPolicyType NEVER stays as the concurrency guard

s1: the baseline is agri-ONLY (drizzle owns geo and tracking, src/lib/server/db/schema.ts:22-23); never edit src/lib/server/db/migration-contract.ts (/api/ready pins the DRIZZLE migration); production moves with `alembic stamp`, never `upgrade`; gate the stamp on an empty `pg_dump --schema-only --schema=agri` diff; tests/test_migration_runtime_contract.py:30-34 asserts the literal 'timescaledb'::text in 20260719_0001 -- rewrite it in the same change; the two alembic pins move in the SAME commit as the revision

s2: direct writers import nothing from agri_data_service.db; days are opaque YYYY-MM-DD strings (PUBLISHER_NAMED_DAY_RULE); source-served-nothing -> write_absence, unreachable -> raise, never a zero-row partition; write_partition refuses a day with absent.json (signal 2026-08-08..16 are pivot d1's to retract); never edit objectstore.py/gap_fill.py (d0) or drain.py (d1)

s3: soil-survey has NO Python producer (rows are warmed by src/lib/server/services/usda-soil.ts) -- decide and record, never silently skip; a static_lookup day is a source VERSION STAMP; burn-severity cadence stays 1; fire-perimeters 2025-08-02..09-30 is a real gap, not an absence

s4: the governed contract is (signal_name, normalized_unit, lane), NULL required_source_key means no lane gate; never re-add min/max/avg (equal to normalized_value on 100% of 701,257 rows, 3.81x larger); cell position is the centroid resolved AFTER the aggregate; observation_count is republish count; pipeline/lanes/signal.py stays untouched until s5; parity sampling must know which layout each sampled z13 day was written in

s5: never delete pipeline/lanes/<slug>.py while pivot d1's drain.py imports the adapters; pipeline/lanes/soil_field.py is d5's; one lane per commit, deletion separate from parity proof; no hand-run DROP against production; interventions stays in Postgres (RUNBOOK 0.26.1)

s6: cannot start until pivot d3 and d4 have shipped; justification is architectural (grep-backed absence of readers + Parquet coverage proof), never an idx_scan counter; uq_signal_observation_release_cell_signal_time is a UNIQUE CONSTRAINT (DROP CONSTRAINT); ix_signal_observation_cell_time_signal (4,163,429 scans) goes LAST; one relation per revision; community features stay in Postgres
